answers.how: Measured the length of the small bird in the video as 55 pixels. Given the prior length of 0.94 m, the scale is 0.94 / 55 = 0.01709 m/pixel. The big bird's length was measured as 89 pixels. Converting this gives 89 * 0.01709 = 1.52 m.
Measured the maximum width (wingspan) of the big bird as 275 pixels. Using the scale of 0.01709 m/pixel from the small bird's length, the big bird's width is 275 * 0.01709 = 4.70 m.
Measured the maximum width (wingspan) of the small bird as 156 pixels. Applying the calculated scale of 0.01709 m/pixel gives 156 * 0.01709 = 2.67 m.

Tracked the small bird's position across 4 frames (from t=0.000s to t=0.167s) and found it moved 96 pixels to the right, yielding a speed of 576 pixels/second. Using the scale 0.01709 m/pixel, its average speed is 576 * 0.01709 = 9.84 m/s.

Tracked the big bird's position across 4 frames and found it moved 236 pixels to the left, yielding a speed of 1416 pixels/second. Converting with the scale 0.01709 m/pixel gives an average speed of 1416 * 0.01709 = 24.20 m/s.

Calculated the positions of both birds at t=0.5 s (frame 12). The initial center-to-center horizontal distance was 251 pixels. With the big bird moving left at 59 px/frame and the small bird moving right at 24 px/frame, they separate by 83 px/frame. After 12 frames, their center-to-center distance is 251 + (12 * 83) = 1247 pixels. Using the scale 0.01709 m/pixel gives 1247 * 0.01709 = 21.31 m.
